drills.solution: Complete the square: add $\left(\tfrac{{D}}{2}\right)^2 = {hh}$ and $\left(\tfrac{{E}}{2}\right)^2 = {kk}$ to both sides of $x^2 {D:signedcoef}x + y^2 {E:signedcoef}y = {nF}$. That gives $(x {nh:signed})^2 + (y {nk:signed})^2 = {r2}$, so the center is **({h}, {k})** and the radius is $\sqrt{{r2}} =$ **{r}**.

drills.title: Area of a trapezoid
drills.prompt: A trapezoid has bases {b1} and {b2} and height {h}. Find its area.
drills.solution: $A = \tfrac12(b_1 + b_2)h = \tfrac12({b1} + {b2})({h}) = \tfrac12 \cdot {s} \cdot {h} =$ **{A}**.

drills.title: Area of a rhombus or kite
drills.prompt: A {shape} has diagonals {d1} and {d2}. Find its area.
drills.solution: The diagonals are perpendicular, so the area is half their product: $\tfrac12 \cdot {d1} \cdot {d2} =$ **{A}**.

drills.title: Triangle area from two sides and an angle
drills.prompt: A triangle has sides {a} and {b} with an included angle of ${C}^\circ$. Find its area (2 decimals).
drills.solution: The height to side {a} is ${b}\sin {C}^\circ$, so $A = \tfrac12 ab\sin C = \tfrac12 \cdot {a} \cdot {b} \cdot \sin {C}^\circ \approx$ **{A:num2}**.

drills.title: Circle area from circumference
drills.prompt: A circle has circumference ${C2}\pi$. Find its area (exact, like 49pi, or 2 decimals).
drills.solution: $2\pi r = {C2}\pi$ gives $r = {r}$. Then $A = \pi r^2 = {r2}\pi \approx$ **{A:num2}**.

drills.title: Sector area
drills.prompt: Find the area of a sector with central angle ${ang}^\circ$ in a circle of radius {r} (exact or 2 decimals).
drills.solution: The sector is $\tfrac{{ang}}{360}$ of the circle: $\dfrac{{ang}}{360} \cdot \pi \cdot {r2} \approx$ **{A:num2}**.

drills.title: Area of a regular polygon
drills.prompt: Find the apothem and the area of a regular {n}-gon with side {s} (2 decimals).
drills.solution: Half the central angle is $\tfrac{180}{{n}} \approx {half:num2}^\circ$. In the right triangle with half a side ($\tfrac{{s}}{2}$) opposite that angle, the apothem is $a = \dfrac{{s}/2}{\tan {half:num2}^\circ} \approx$ **{a:num2}**. Perimeter $P = {n} \cdot {s} = {P}$, so $A = \tfrac12 aP \approx$ **{A:num2}**.

drills.title: Surface area of a box
drills.prompt: Find the surface area of a rectangular prism {l} by {w} by {h}.
drills.solution: Three pairs of faces: $2({l} \cdot {w} + {l} \cdot {h} + {w} \cdot {h}) = 2({lw} + {lh} + {wh}) =$ **{S}**.

drills.title: Surface area of a cylinder
drills.prompt: A cylinder has radius {r} and height {h}. Find its lateral area and total surface area (exact like 48pi, or 2 decimals).
drills.solution: Lateral area $= 2\pi rh = {kL:dp0}\pi \approx$ **{L:num2}**. Adding the two bases ($2\pi r^2 = {kB:dp0}\pi$): $S = {k:dp0}\pi \approx$ **{S:num2}**.

drills.title: Surface area of a cone
drills.prompt: A right cone has radius {r} and height {h}. Find its slant height and total surface area (2 decimals).
drills.solution: The slant height is the hypotenuse of the right triangle with legs $r$ and $h$: $\ell = \sqrt{{r}^2 + {h}^2} = \sqrt{{l2}} \approx$ **{l:num2}**. Then $S = \pi r\ell + \pi r^2 \approx$ **{S:num2}**.

drills.title: Volume of a cone
drills.prompt: Find the volume of a cone with radius {r} and height {h} (2 decimals).
drills.solution: $V = \tfrac13 \pi r^2 h = \tfrac13 \pi \cdot {r}^2 \cdot {h} \approx$ **{V:num2}**.

drills.title: Volume of a square pyramid from its slant height
drills.prompt: A square pyramid has base edge {s} and slant height $\ell = \sqrt{{l2}}$. Find its height and its volume (2 decimals if needed).
drills.solution: The height, half the base edge ({hb}) and the slant height form a right triangle: $h = \sqrt{\ell^2 - {hb}^2} = \sqrt{{l2} - {hb2}} =$ **{h}**. Then $V = \tfrac13 Bh = \tfrac13 \cdot {s2} \cdot {h} \approx$ **{V:num2}**.

drills.title: Sphere from its volume
drills.prompt: A sphere has volume $\tfrac{{k:dp0}}{3}\pi$. Find its radius and its surface area (2 decimals).
drills.solution: $\tfrac43 \pi r^3 = \tfrac{{k:dp0}}{3}\pi$ gives $4r^3 = {k:dp0}$, so $r^3 = {k:dp0}/4$ and $r =$ **{r}**. Then $S = 4\pi r^2 \approx$ **{S:num2}**.

drills.title: Volume of a cylinder
drills.prompt: A cylinder has radius {r} and height {h}. Find its volume (exact like 48pi, or 2 decimals).
drills.solution: $V = Bh = \pi r^2 h = \pi({r})^2({h}) = {kV:dp0}\pi \approx$ **{V:num2}**.

drills.title: Surface area of a solid of revolution
drills.prompt: A right triangle with legs {lp} and {lq} is spun around the leg of length {lq}. Name the radius of the solid it sweeps out, then find the solid's total surface area (2 decimals).
drills.solution:
Spinning a right triangle about a leg makes a cone. The leg it spins around is the height ({lq}), the other leg is the radius, $r =$ **{lp}**, and the hypotenuse becomes the slant height: $\ell = \sqrt{{lp}^2 + {lq}^2} = \sqrt{{l2}} \approx {l:num2}$.
Total surface area $= \pi r^2 + \pi r\ell = \pi({lp})^2 + \pi({lp})(\sqrt{{l2}}) \approx$ **{S:num2}**.

drills.title: Distance between two points
drills.prompt: Find the distance between $({x1}, {y1})$ and $({x2}, {y2})$ (exact or 2 decimals).
drills.solution: The legs are $|\Delta x| = |{dx}|$ and $|\Delta y| = |{dy}|$, so $d = \sqrt{({dx})^2 + ({dy})^2} = \sqrt{{s}} \approx$ **{d:num2}**.

drills.title: Midpoint and missing endpoint
drills.prompt: $M({mx}, {my})$ is the midpoint of $\overline{AB}$, and $A = ({ax}, {ay})$. Find $B$.
drills.solution: Going from $A$ to $M$ changes $x$ by ${sx}$ and $y$ by ${sy}$. Do the same again from $M$: $B = ({mx} {sx:signed}, {my} {sy:signed}) =$ **({bx}, {by})**. (Equivalently $\tfrac{{ax} + x}{2} = {mx}$ and $\tfrac{{ay} + y}{2} = {my}$.)

drills.title: Partition a segment in a ratio
drills.prompt: Find the point $P$ on $\overline{AB}$ with $A({x1}, {y1})$ and $B({x2}, {y2})$ such that $AP : PB = {m} : {n}$.
drills.solution: $P$ is $k = \tfrac{{m}}{{m} + {n}} = \tfrac{{m}}{{t}}$ of the way from $A$ to $B$. The changes are $\Delta x = {dx}$ and $\Delta y = {dy}$, so $P = \left({x1} + \tfrac{{m}}{{t}}({dx}),\; {y1} + \tfrac{{m}}{{t}}({dy})\right) =$ **({px}, {py})**.

drills.title: Translate a point
drills.prompt: Translate $({x}, {y})$ by $\langle {a}, {b} \rangle$.
drills.solution: Add the vector to the point: $({x} {a:signed}, {y} {b:signed}) =$ **({x2}, {y2})**.

drills.title: Reflect a point
drills.prompt: Reflect the point $({x}, {y})$ in {L}.
drills.solution: Rules: $x$-axis $(x, -y)$; $y$-axis $(-x, y)$; $y = x$ swaps to $(y, x)$; $y = -x$ gives $(-y, -x)$. Reflecting in {L} gives **({x2}, {y2})**.

drills.title: Rotate a point about the origin
drills.prompt: Rotate $({x}, {y})$ by ${ang}^\circ$ counterclockwise about the origin.
drills.solution: Counterclockwise about the origin: $90^\circ$ gives $(-y, x)$, $180^\circ$ gives $(-x, -y)$, $270^\circ$ gives $(y, -x)$. For ${ang}^\circ$ the image is **({x2}, {y2})**.

drills.title: Dilate about a point
drills.prompt: Dilate $P({px}, {py})$ with center $C({cx}, {cy})$ and scale factor ${k}$.
drills.solution: Relative to $C$, $P$ is at $({dx}, {dy})$. Scale by ${k}$: $({kdx}, {kdy})$. Add $C$ back: $P' =$ **({qx}, {qy})**.

drills.title: Compose two transformations
drills.prompt: Rotate $({x}, {y})$ by $90^\circ$ counterclockwise about the origin, then translate the image by $\langle {a}, {b} \rangle$. Where does the point end up?
drills.solution: Rotate first: $(x, y) \to (-y, x)$ gives $({rx}, {ry})$. Then translate: $({rx} {a:signed}, {ry} {b:signed}) =$ **({fx}, {fy})**.

drills.title: Symmetry of regular polygons
drills.prompt: A regular polygon has {n} sides. How many lines of symmetry does it have, and what is the smallest positive angle of rotation (in degrees) that maps it onto itself? (2 decimals if needed)
drills.solution: A regular $n$-gon has $n$ lines of symmetry (**{n}**) and rotational symmetry of $360^\circ / n = \tfrac{360}{{n}} \approx$ **{ang:num2}°**.

drills.title: Parabola from focus and directrix
drills.prompt: A parabola has focus $({h}, {fy})$ and directrix $y = {dy}$. Write its equation solved for $y$.
drills.solution:
The vertex is halfway between the focus and the directrix: $({h}, {k})$. The focus is $p = {p}$ units from the vertex (negative means below), so $4p = {fp}$ and
$(x {nh:signed})^2 = {fp}(y {nk:signed})$.
Solve for $y$: $y =$ **${aa:texfrac}(x {nh:signed})^2 {k:signed}$**.

drills.title: Focus and directrix from an equation
drills.prompt: Find the focus and directrix of $y = {a}(x {nh:signed})^2 {k:signed}$.
drills.solution:
The vertex is $({h}, {k})$. For $y = a(x - h)^2 + k$, $p = \dfrac{1}{4a}$, so $p = {p:num4}$ (positive: the parabola opens up; negative: down).
Focus: $({h}, {k} {p:signed}) =$ **({h}, {fy:num4})**. Directrix: $y = {k} - ({p:num4})$, that is, **$y = {dy:num4}$**.

drills.title: The similarity between two circles
drills.prompt: Circle $C_1$ is $(x {nh1:signed})^2 + (y {nk1:signed})^2 = {q1}$ and circle $C_2$ is $(x {nh2:signed})^2 + (y {nk2:signed})^2 = {q2}$. A translation by $\langle a, b \rangle$, followed by a dilation centered at the new center with scale factor $k$, maps $C_1$ onto $C_2$. Find $a$, $b$ and $k$ ($k$ as a fraction or 2 decimals).
drills.solution:
$C_1$ has center $({h1}, {k1})$ and radius $\sqrt{{q1}} = {r1}$; $C_2$ has center $({h2}, {k2})$ and radius $\sqrt{{q2}} = {r2}$.
The translation moves center to center: $\langle {h2} - ({h1}),\; {k2} - ({k1}) \rangle =$ **$\langle {ta}, {tb} \rangle$**.
The dilation scales the radius from {r1} to {r2}: $k = \tfrac{{r2}}{{r1}} \approx$ **{kk:num2}**.

drills.title: Multiply with parallel lines
drills.prompt: On one side of an angle with vertex $O$, points $U$ and $B$ have $OU = {u}$ and $OB = {bv}$. On the other side, $OA = {av}$. The line through $B$ parallel to $\overline{UA}$ meets the second side at $P$. Find $OP$.
drills.solution: $\overline{BP} \parallel \overline{UA}$, so $\triangle OUA \sim \triangle OBP$ and $\dfrac{OP}{OA} = \dfrac{OB}{OU}$. So $OP = {av} \cdot \dfrac{ {bv} }{ {u} } =$ **{op}**. (With $OU = 1$ this construction multiplies: $OP = OA \cdot OB$.)

drills.title: Square root from a semicircle
drills.prompt: Points $A$, $B$, $C$ lie on a line in that order with $AB = {p}$ and $BC = {q}$. A semicircle is drawn on diameter $\overline{AC}$, and the perpendicular to $\overline{AC}$ at $B$ meets it at $D$. Find $BD$. Give the exact value (such as sqrt(10)) or a decimal to 2 places.
drills.solution: $\angle ADC$ is inscribed in a semicircle, so it is a right angle, and $\overline{DB}$ is the altitude to the hypotenuse. It is the geometric mean of the pieces: $BD = \sqrt{AB \cdot BC} = \sqrt{ {pq} } \approx$ **{h:num2}**.

drills.title: Ceva's theorem, find the third ratio
drills.prompt: In $\triangle ABC$, cevians $\overline{AD}$, $\overline{BE}$ and $\overline{CF}$ are concurrent, with $D$ on $\overline{BC}$, $E$ on $\overline{CA}$ and $F$ on $\overline{AB}$. $AF = {af}$, $FB = {fb}$, $BD = {bd}$, $DC = {dc}$ and $CA = {ca}$. Find $CE$ and $EA$.
drills.solution: Ceva: $\dfrac{AF}{FB} \cdot \dfrac{BD}{DC} \cdot \dfrac{CE}{EA} = 1$, so $\dfrac{CE}{EA} = \dfrac{FB \cdot DC}{AF \cdot BD} = \dfrac{ {num} }{ {den} } = \dfrac{ {pp} }{ {qq} }$. Split $CA = {ca}$ in the ratio ${pp} : {qq}$: $CE =$ **{ce}** and $EA =$ **{ea}**.

drills.title: Menelaus's theorem with an extended side
drills.prompt: A line crosses side $\overline{AB}$ of $\triangle ABC$ at $F$, side $\overline{AC}$ at $E$, and the extension of $\overline{BC}$ beyond $C$ at $D$. $AF = {af}$, $FB = {fb}$, $BC = {bc}$, $CD = {cd}$ and $AC = {ac}$. Find $CE$ and $EA$.
drills.solution: $D$ is beyond $C$, so $BD = {bc} + {cd} = {bd}$. Menelaus: $\dfrac{AF}{FB} \cdot \dfrac{BD}{DC} \cdot \dfrac{CE}{EA} = 1$, so $\dfrac{CE}{EA} = \dfrac{FB \cdot DC}{AF \cdot BD} = \dfrac{ {fb} \cdot {cd} }{ {af} \cdot {bd} } = \dfrac{ {pp} }{ {qq} }$. Split $AC = {ac}$ in the ratio ${pp} : {qq}$: $CE =$ **{ce}** and $EA =$ **{ea}**.

drills.title: Centroid and nine-point center from O and H
drills.prompt: A triangle has circumcenter $O({ox}, {oy})$ and orthocenter $H({hx}, {hy})$. Find its centroid $G$ and its nine-point center $N$. (Decimals such as 2.5 are fine.)
drills.solution: On the Euler line $G$ is one-third of the way from $O$ to $H$, so $G = \tfrac{H + 2O}{3} = \left(\tfrac{({hx}) + 2({ox})}{3},\ \tfrac{({hy}) + 2({oy})}{3}\right) = \left(\tfrac{ {sx} }{3}, \tfrac{ {sy} }{3}\right) =$ **({cgx}, {cgy})**. The nine-point center is the midpoint of $\overline{OH}$: $N = \left(\tfrac{({ox}) + ({hx})}{2}, \tfrac{({oy}) + ({hy})}{2}\right) =$ **({nx}, {ny})**.

drills.title: Euler line of a right triangle
drills.prompt: A right triangle has legs {la} and {lb}. Find the distance $OH$ from its circumcenter to its orthocenter, the distance $OG$ from its circumcenter to its centroid, and the radius of its nine-point circle. Give exact values or decimals to 2 places.
drills.solution: The hypotenuse is $\sqrt{ {la}^2 + {lb}^2 } = {hyp}$. The circumcenter $O$ is its midpoint, so $R = {oh}$, and the orthocenter $H$ is the right-angle vertex. $OH$ is the median to the hypotenuse, which is half the hypotenuse: $OH =$ **{oh}**. Then $OG = \tfrac13 OH = \tfrac{ {oh} }{3} \approx$ **{og:num2}** and the nine-point radius is $\tfrac R2 =$ **{rn}**.

drills.title: Diagonal of an isosceles trapezoid by Ptolemy
drills.prompt: An isosceles trapezoid has bases {b1} and {b2} and legs {leg}. Use Ptolemy's theorem to find the length of a diagonal. Give the exact value (such as sqrt(97)) or a decimal to 2 places.
drills.solution: An isosceles trapezoid is cyclic and its diagonals are congruent; call each $d$. The opposite sides are the bases and the legs, so Ptolemy gives $d \cdot d = {b1} \cdot {b2} + {leg} \cdot {leg} = {prod} + {lsq} = {dd}$. So $d = \sqrt{ {dd} } \approx$ **{d:num2}**.

drills.title: Area of a cyclic quadrilateral
where: 2*max(sa, sb, sc, sd) < sa + sb + sc + sd
drills.prompt: A cyclic quadrilateral has sides {sa}, {sb}, {sc} and {sd}. Use Brahmagupta's formula to find its area to 2 decimal places.
drills.solution: Semiperimeter $s = \tfrac{ {sa} + {sb} + {sc} + {sd} }{2} = {s}$. Then $K = \sqrt{(s - a)(s - b)(s - c)(s - d)} = \sqrt{ {pa} \cdot {pb} \cdot {pc} \cdot {pd} } = \sqrt{ {prod:dp0} } \approx$ **{area:num2}**.

drills.title: A point on the circumcircle of an equilateral triangle
drills.prompt: Equilateral triangle $ABC$ is inscribed in a circle. $P$ is on arc $BC$ (the arc not containing $A$), with $PB = {pb}$ and $PC = {pc}$. Find $PA$, and the side length of the triangle (exact, such as sqrt(49), or to 2 decimal places).
drills.solution: Ptolemy in cyclic quadrilateral $ABPC$: $PA \cdot BC = AB \cdot PC + AC \cdot PB$. All three sides equal $s$, so dividing by $s$ gives $PA = PB + PC =$ **{pa}**. For the side, $\angle BPC$ is inscribed in a $240^\circ$ arc, so it measures $120^\circ$, and the Law of Cosines gives $s^2 = {pb}^2 + {pc}^2 - 2({pb})({pc})\cos 120^\circ = {ssq}$. So $s = \sqrt{ {ssq} } \approx$ **{side:num2}**.

drills.title: Which side of a line? Where does a segment cross?
drills.prompt: Line $\ell$ is $y = {m:coef}x {b:signed}$. Let $d = y - ({m:coef}x {b:signed})$. Find $d$ at $P({p1}, {p2})$ and at $Q({q1}, {q2})$, then the $x$-coordinate of the point where $\overline{PQ}$ crosses $\ell$ (as a fraction, or a decimal to 2 places).
drills.solution: At $P$: $d_P = {p2} - ({mp}) = {dP}$. At $Q$: $d_Q = {q2} - ({mq}) = {dQ}$. The signs are opposite, so $P$ and $Q$ are on opposite sides of $\ell$ and $\overline{PQ}$ crosses it. The crossing is the fraction $t = \dfrac{d_P}{d_P - d_Q} = \dfrac{{dP}}{{s}}$ of the way from $P$ to $Q$, so $x = {p1} + {t:texfrac}\,({q1} - ({p1})) =$ **${xc:texfrac}$** (about {xc:num2}). Check: there $y = {yc:texfrac}$, which is on $\ell$.

drills.title: Lines through points, some collinear
drills.prompt: There are {n} points. Exactly {k} of them lie on one line, and no other three of the points are collinear. How many lines pass through at least two of the points?
drills.solution: With no three collinear there would be $\binom{{n}}{2} = {all}$ lines. The {k} collinear points form $\binom{{k}}{2} = {extra}$ pairs that all give the same line, so that line was counted {extra} times instead of once: ${all} - {extra} + 1 =$ **{lines}**.

drills.title: Regions made by lines in general position
drills.prompt: {n} lines are drawn in a plane, no two parallel and no three through one point. Find the number of crossing points, the number of regions, and the number of bounded regions.
drills.solution: Every pair of lines meets once: $\binom{{n}}{2} =$ **{pts}** points. Regions: $\dfrac{n^2 + n + 2}{2} = \dfrac{{nsq} + {n} + 2}{2} =$ **{reg}**. There are $2n = {unb}$ unbounded regions, so bounded $= {reg} - {unb} =$ **{bnd}** (the same as $\binom{n-1}{2}$).

drills.title: Angles formed by concurrent lines
drills.prompt: {n} lines pass through one point, with equal angles between neighboring rays. How many angles are formed (not counting straight angles), how many pairs of vertical angles are there, and what is the smallest angle in degrees (to 2 decimal places if needed)?
drills.solution: The lines make {rays} rays. Of the $\binom{{rays}}{2} = {rp}$ pairs of rays, {n} pairs are opposite rays (straight angles), leaving ${rp} - {n} =$ **{ang}** angles. Each has one vertical partner, so there are ${ang} \div 2 =$ **{vp}** vertical pairs. The {rays} equal angles around the point are $\dfrac{360^\circ}{{rays}} =$ **{small:num2}°**.

drills.title: Counting in a projective plane
drills.prompt: A finite projective plane has order {n}. How many points are on each line, how many points does the plane have, and how many lines does it have?
drills.solution: Order {n} means each line has $n + 1 =$ **{k}** points. Fix a point $P$: it is on {k} lines, each holding {n} other points, and every other point is on exactly one of them. So there are $1 + {k} \cdot {n} = {n2} + {n} + 1 =$ **{N}** points. By duality (or the same count with points and lines swapped) there are also **{N}** lines.

drills.title: From a projective plane to an affine plane
drills.prompt: A projective plane has {N} points and {N} lines, with {k} points on each line. One line and all its points are deleted. How many points and lines are left, and how many lines are in each parallel class of the resulting affine plane?
drills.solution: The plane has order $n = {k} - 1 = {n}$. Deleting a line removes its {k} points, leaving ${N} - {k} =$ **{P}** points, and removes one line, leaving ${N} - 1 =$ **{L}** lines. The {k} deleted points give {k} parallel classes, and each deleted point was on {k} lines, one of which was the deleted line, so each class has **{n}** lines.

drills.title: Splitting a hyperbolic triangle
drills.prompt: In hyperbolic geometry, $\triangle ABC$ has $\angle A = {A}^\circ$, $\angle B = {B}^\circ$ and $\angle C = {C}^\circ$. A segment from $A$ to a point $D$ on $\overline{BC}$ makes $\angle BAD = {a1}^\circ$, and then $\angle ADB = {D1}^\circ$ (to the nearest degree). Find the defects of $\triangle ABC$, $\triangle ABD$ and $\triangle ADC$, in degrees.
drills.solution: Whole triangle: $180 - ({A} + {B} + {C}) =$ **{whole}°**. In $\triangle ABD$ the angles are ${a1}^\circ$, ${B}^\circ$, ${D1}^\circ$, sum ${s1}^\circ$, so its defect is **{def1}°**. In $\triangle ADC$: $\angle DAC = {A} - {a1} = {a2}^\circ$ and $\angle ADC = 180 - {D1} = {D2}^\circ$ (a linear pair), with $\angle C = {C}^\circ$; the sum is ${s2}^\circ$ and the defect is **{def2}°**. Check: ${def1} + {def2} = {whole}$, because defect is additive. (In hyperbolic geometry the angles of a triangle determine it, so $\angle ADB$ is not free to choose: it was computed from the other angles with hyperbolic trigonometry.)

drills.title: Angles of a Saccheri quadrilateral
drills.prompt: In hyperbolic geometry, a Saccheri quadrilateral has summit angles of ${s}^\circ$ each. Find its angle sum, its defect ($360^\circ$ minus the angle sum), and the defect of each Lambert quadrilateral formed by cutting it along the segment joining the midpoints of the base and the summit.
drills.solution: The base angles are right angles, so the sum is $90 + 90 + {s} + {s} =$ **{total}°**, and the defect is $360 - {total} =$ **{dq}°**. Each half has angles $90^\circ$, $90^\circ$, $90^\circ$ and ${s}^\circ$, so its defect is $360 - (270 + {s}) =$ **{dl}°**, half of the whole.

drills.title: Buffon's needle probability
drills.prompt: A needle {l} cm long is dropped on a floor ruled with parallel lines {d} cm apart. What is the probability that it crosses a line? Give 3 decimal places.
drills.solution: Since $\ell = {l} \le d = {d}$, Buffon's formula applies: $P = \dfrac{2\ell}{\pi d} = \dfrac{{l2}}{{d}\pi} \approx$ **{p:dp3}**.

drills.title: Estimating pi with needles
drills.prompt: A needle {l} cm long is dropped {N} times on lines {d} cm apart and crosses a line {C} times. Estimate $\pi$ from this experiment. Give 3 decimal places.
drills.solution: The fraction of drops that cross, {C} out of {N}, estimates $\tfrac{2\ell}{\pi d}$, so $\pi \approx \dfrac{2\ell N}{d\,C} = \dfrac{2 \cdot {l} \cdot {N}}{{d} \cdot {C}} = \dfrac{{top}}{{bot}} \approx$ **{est:dp3}**.

drills.title: Random chords three ways
drills.prompt: In a circle of radius {r}, a chord is chosen at random. Find the probability that the chord is longer than {L}, using each of Bertrand's methods: (1) two random endpoints on the circle, (2) a random point on a random radius, (3) a random midpoint in the disk. Give 3 decimal places.
drills.solution:
A chord at distance $t$ from the center has length $2\sqrt{r^2 - t^2}$, so it is longer than {L} when $t < \sqrt{{r}^2 - {h}^2} \approx {t:num4}$.

(1) A chord of central angle $\varphi$ has length $2r\sin\tfrac{\varphi}{2}$, which equals {L} at $\varphi \approx {ang:num2}^\circ$. The second endpoint must be more than that far from the first in either direction: $P = 1 - \tfrac{2 \cdot {ang:num2}}{360} \approx$ **{p1:dp3}**.

(2) $t$ is uniform on $[0, {r}]$: $P = \tfrac{{t:num4}}{{r}} \approx$ **{p2:dp3}**.

(3) The midpoint must land within ${t:num4}$ of the center: $P = \left(\tfrac{{t:num4}}{{r}}\right)^2 \approx$ **{p3:dp3}**.

drills.title: Sum of consecutive odd numbers
drills.prompt: Find the sum $1 + 3 + 5 + \dots + {last}$.
drills.solution: The last term is $2n - 1 = {last}$, so there are $n = {n}$ odd numbers. The sum of the first $n$ odd numbers is $n^2$, so the sum is ${n}^2 =$ **{S}**.

drills.title: Sum of odd numbers that starts later
drills.prompt: Find the sum of the odd numbers ${first} + {second} + \dots + {last}$.
drills.solution: $1 + 3 + \dots + {last}$ is the sum of the first {b} odd numbers (since $2 \cdot {b} - 1 = {last}$), which is ${b}^2 = {B2}$. The odd numbers below {first} are $1 + 3 + \dots + {below}$, the first {a} odd numbers, with sum ${a}^2 = {A2}$. So the sum is ${B2} - {A2} =$ **{S}**.

drills.title: The bend theorem with algebra
drills.prompt: $\ell \parallel m$. A path runs from $A$ on $\ell$ to a point $P$ between the lines and on to $B$ on $m$. The angles at $A$ and $B$ between the path and the lines, on the side toward the bend, measure $({c1:coef}x {d1:signed})^\circ$ and $({c2:coef}x {d2:signed})^\circ$, and $m\angle APB = ({c3}x {d3:signed})^\circ$. Find $x$ and $m\angle APB$.
drills.solution: Draw the auxiliary line through $P$ parallel to $\ell$ and $m$ (dashed). It splits $\angle APB$ into two alternate-interior copies of the angles at $A$ and $B$, so $m\angle APB$ is their sum: ${c3}x {d3:signed} = ({c1:coef}x {d1:signed}) + ({c2:coef}x {d2:signed}) = {cs}x {ds:signed}$. Then ${k:coef}x = {rhs}$, so $x =$ **{x}**, and $m\angle APB = {angA} + {angB} =$ **{bend}°**.

drills.title: Zigzag between parallel lines
drills.prompt: $\ell \parallel m$. A path leaves $A$ on $\ell$ heading down to the right, making a ${a}^\circ$ angle with $\ell$ (opening right). It bends at $P$ with an angle of ${p}^\circ$ (opening left), bends again at $Q$ with an angle of ${q}^\circ$ (opening right), and reaches $B$ on $m$. Find the acute angle $x$ between the path and $m$ at $B$, in degrees.
drills.solution: The angle at $B$ opens to the left. By the zigzag rule (draw a parallel through $P$ and through $Q$), the angles opening right total the same as those opening left: ${a} + {q} = {p} + x$, so $x =$ **{ans}°**. Check: the segments make ${t1}^\circ$, ${p} - {t1} = {t2}^\circ$ and ${q} - {t2} = {t3}^\circ$ with the parallels, and the last one meets $m$ at ${t3}^\circ$.

drills.title: Angle between two lines
drills.prompt: Find the angle between the lines $y = {m1:coef}x {b1:signed}$ and $y = {m2:coef}x {b2:signed}$, in degrees to the nearest tenth.
drills.solution: Direction vectors: $\langle 1, {m1} \rangle$ and $\langle 1, {m2} \rangle$. Dot product: $1 + ({m1})({m2}) = {dot}$. Lengths: $\sqrt{{n1}}$ and $\sqrt{{n2}}$. So $\cos\varphi = \dfrac{|{dot}|}{\sqrt{{n1}}\,\sqrt{{n2}}}$, and $\varphi \approx$ **{angr}°**.

drills.title: Foot of the perpendicular
drills.prompt: Find the foot of the perpendicular from $P({x0}, {y0})$ to the line ${A:coef}x {B:signedcoef}y {C:signed} = 0$.
drills.solution: Here $A = {A}$, $B = {B}$, $C = {C}$. Then $Ax_0 + By_0 + C = {v}$ and $A^2 + B^2 = {N2}$, so $t = -\dfrac{{v}}{{N2}} = {t}$. Move from $P$ along the normal vector $\langle {A}, {B} \rangle$: $F = ({x0} + ({t})({A}),\ {y0} + ({t})({B})) =$ **({fx}, {fy})**. Check: ${A}({fx}) + {B}({fy}) {C:signed} = 0$.

drills.title: Distance between parallel lines
drills.prompt: Find the distance between the parallel lines ${A}x {B:signedcoef}y = {c1}$ and ${kA}x {kB:signedcoef}y = {c2}$. (Exact, or 2 decimals.)
drills.solution: First make sure both equations have the same $A$ and $B$ (divide the second by {k} if needed): ${A}x {B:signedcoef}y = {c2b}$. For $Ax + By = c_1$ and $Ax + By = c_2$ the distance is $\dfrac{|c_1 - c_2|}{\sqrt{A^2 + B^2}} = \dfrac{|{c1} - ({c2b})|}{\sqrt{({A})^2 + ({B})^2}} = \dfrac{{diff}}{{N}} \approx$ **{d:num4}**.

drills.title: Exterior angle at the vertex of an isosceles triangle
drills.prompt: In an isosceles triangle, one leg is extended past the vertex angle. The exterior angle formed there measures ${ext}^\circ$. Find each base angle and the vertex angle, in degrees.
drills.solution: The exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles, which are the two equal base angles: $2b = {ext}$, so each base angle is $b =$ **{base}°**. The vertex angle forms a linear pair with the exterior angle: $180 - {ext} =$ **{vert}°**. Check: ${base} + {base} + {vert} = 180$.

drills.title: How many triangles from SSA?
drills.prompt: $\angle A$ is acute, $AC = {b}$, and $C$ is ${d}$ units from the other side of $\angle A$. How many different triangles $ABC$ have $BC = {a}$? (Count two triangles as the same only if they are congruent.)
drills.solution: Compare $a = {a}$ with $d = {d}$ and $b = {b}$. If $a < d$ the circle of radius $a$ around $C$ misses the other side: none. If $a = d$ it touches once: one right triangle. If $d < a < b$ it crosses the ray twice: two triangles. If $a \ge b$ the second crossing is at $A$ or behind it: one triangle. Here the answer is **{n}**.

drills.title: The two SSA triangles
drills.prompt: In the SSA construction with an acute $\angle A$, the perpendicular from $C$ to the other side of the angle lands at $F$, with $AF = {p}$ and $CF = {d}$. If $BC = {a}$, find the two possible lengths of $\overline{AB}$.
drills.solution: The two possible positions of $B$ are the same distance from $F$, one on each side. By the Pythagorean theorem that distance is $\sqrt{ {a}^2 - {d}^2 } = {k}$. Both lie on the ray because ${k} < {p}$. So $AB = {p} - {k} =$ **{short}** or $AB = {p} + {k} =$ **{long}**.

drills.title: Range for the fourth side of a quadrilateral
drills.prompt: Three sides of a quadrilateral are {p}, {q} and {r}. The fourth side $s$ satisfies $L < s < U$. Find $L$ and $U$.
drills.solution: Each side must be shorter than the sum of the other three. If $s$ is longest: $s < {p} + {q} + {r} = {hi}$. If {r} is longest: ${r} < {p} + {q} + s$, so $s > {r} - {p} - {q} = {lo}$. So **{lo}** $< s <$ **{hi}**.

drills.title: Shortest path by way of a line
drills.prompt: A path starts at $A(0, {ya})$, touches the $x$-axis at a point $P$, and ends at $B({xb}, {yb})$. Find the $x$-coordinate of the point $P$ that makes the path shortest, and the shortest length (to 2 decimal places).
drills.solution: Reflect $A$ across the $x$-axis to $A'(0, -{ya})$. The best $P$ is where segment $\overline{A'B}$ crosses the axis. That segment rises ${s}$ over a run of ${xb}$, and it must rise ${ya}$ to reach the axis, so $x = {xb} \cdot \dfrac{ {ya} }{ {s} } =$ **{xp}**. The shortest length is $A'B = \sqrt{ {xb}^2 + {s}^2 } \approx$ **{plen:num2}**.

drills.title: Orthocenter from coordinates
drills.prompt: Find the orthocenter $H$ of the triangle with vertices $A({xa}, 0)$, $B({xb}, 0)$ and $C({xc}, {ht})$.
drills.solution: Side $\overline{AB}$ lies on the $x$-axis, so the altitude from $C$ is the vertical line $x = {xc}$. Side $\overline{BC}$ has slope $\dfrac{{ht}}{{xc} - {xb}} = {ms:texfrac}$, so the altitude from $A$, perpendicular to it, has slope ${ma:texfrac}$ and passes through $A({xa}, 0)$: $y = {ma:texfrac}\,(x {nxa:signed})$. At $x = {xc}$, $y = {ma:texfrac} \cdot ({dca}) = {hy}$. So $H =$ **({xc}, {hy})**. (It is outside the triangle exactly when the triangle is obtuse.)

drills.title: Orthocenter from the Euler line
drills.prompt: A triangle has circumcenter $O({ox}, {oy})$ and centroid $G({gx}, {gy})$. Find its orthocenter $H$.
drills.solution: The centroid is one-third of the way from $O$ to $H$, so $3G = H + 2O$ and $H = 3G - 2O$. In $x$: $3({gx}) - 2({ox}) = {hx}$. In $y$: $3({gy}) - 2({oy}) = {hy}$. So $H =$ **({hx}, {hy})**. Check: going from $O$ to $G$ changes the coordinates by $({dx}, {dy})$, and going from $G$ to $H$ changes them by $({dx2}, {dy2})$, twice as much in the same direction.

drills.title: Varignon parallelogram perimeter and area
drills.prompt: Quadrilateral $ABCD$ has vertices $A(0, 0)$, $B({bx}, 0)$, $C({cx}, {cy})$ and $D({dx}, {dy})$, and its area is {K}. Find the perimeter (to 2 decimal places) and the area of its Varignon parallelogram, the parallelogram whose vertices are the midpoints of the sides.
drills.solution: Each side of the Varignon parallelogram is half a diagonal, and there are two sides for each diagonal, so its perimeter is $AC + BD$. $AC = \sqrt{{cx}^2 + {cy}^2} \approx {ac:num2}$ and $BD = \sqrt{({dx} - {bx})^2 + {dy}^2} \approx {bd:num2}$, so the perimeter is about **{per:num2}**. Its area is half the quadrilateral's: $\tfrac12 \cdot {K} =$ **{va}**.

drills.title: Tip angles of a star polygon
drills.prompt: Find each tip angle of the star polygon $\{{n}/{k}\}$ (to 2 decimal places if needed) and the sum of its {n} tip angles, in degrees.
drills.solution: Walking once around $\{{n}/{k}\}$ you circle the center {k} times, so you turn $360^\circ \cdot {k}$ in all, in {n} equal turns of $\dfrac{360^\circ \cdot {k}}{{n}}$ each. Each tip angle is what's left of a straight angle: $180^\circ - \dfrac{360^\circ \cdot {k}}{{n}} =$ **{tip}°** (rounded to 2 decimal places if needed). The {n} tips add to $180({n} - 2 \cdot {k}) =$ **{tsum}°**.

drills.title: The third polygon at a vertex
drills.prompt: A regular polygon with {p} sides and a regular polygon with {q} sides meet at a point. One more regular polygon fills the rest of the $360^\circ$ around the point exactly. How many sides does it have?
drills.solution: For three regular polygons with $a$, $b$ and $c$ sides around a point, $\tfrac1a + \tfrac1b + \tfrac1c = \tfrac12$. So $\tfrac1c = \tfrac12 - \tfrac1{{p}} - \tfrac1{{q}} = {inv:texfrac}$, and $c =$ **{r}**. Check with the angles (rounded to 2 decimal places where needed): ${a1}^\circ + {a2}^\circ + {a3}^\circ = 360^\circ$. (Fitting around one point does not guarantee that a whole tiling exists.)

drills.title: Euclid's formula for Pythagorean triples
drills.prompt: Use Euclid's formula with $m = {m}$ and $n = {n}$ to find the Pythagorean triple $a = m^2 - n^2$, $b = 2mn$, $c = m^2 + n^2$.
drills.solution:
$a = {m}^2 - {n}^2 =$ **{a}**, $b = 2({m})({n}) =$ **{b}**, $c = {m}^2 + {n}^2 =$ **{c}**.
Check: ${a}^2 + {b}^2 = {asq} + {bsq} = {csq} = {c}^2$. The triple is primitive exactly when {m} and {n} share no factor and one of them is even.

drills.title: Similar figures on the sides of a right triangle
drills.prompt: A right triangle has legs {a} and {b}. Semicircles are drawn outward on all three sides, each with a side as its diameter. Find the area of the semicircle on the hypotenuse (2 decimals).
drills.solution:
A semicircle with diameter $s$ has area $\tfrac{\pi}{8}s^2$. The hypotenuse satisfies $c^2 = {a}^2 + {b}^2 = {csq}$, so the area is $\tfrac{\pi}{8}({csq}) \approx$ **{s3:num2}**.
Check with the generalized theorem: the semicircles on the legs have areas $\approx {s1:num2}$ and $\approx {s2:num2}$, which add to the same total.

drills.title: Height from two angles of elevation
drills.prompt: From point $P$ the angle of elevation to a mountain peak is ${al}^\circ$. After walking {d} m straight toward the peak on level ground, the angle of elevation is ${be}^\circ$. How high is the peak above the ground, to the nearest tenth of a meter?
drills.solution:
The angle at the peak is ${be}^\circ - {al}^\circ = {top}^\circ$. Law of Sines for the sight line from the nearer point: $QT = \dfrac{{d}\sin {al}^\circ}{\sin {top}^\circ} \approx {qt:num2}$ m.
Then $h = QT\sin {be}^\circ \approx$ **{h:num1}** m.

drills.title: Two-leg journey on bearings
drills.prompt: A ship sails {r1} km on a bearing of ${t1}^\circ$, then {r2} km on a bearing of ${t2}^\circ$. Find its distance from the start (2 decimals) and the bearing of its position from the start (nearest tenth of a degree).
drills.solution:
**Angle at the turn.** The back bearing of the first leg is ${t1}^\circ + 180^\circ$, and the second leg is on ${t2}^\circ$, so the angle between the legs at the turning point is $180^\circ - {turn}^\circ = {angB}^\circ$.
**Distance.** Law of Cosines: $d^2 = {r1}^2 + {r2}^2 - 2({r1})({r2})\cos {angB}^\circ$, so $d \approx$ **{dist:num2}** km.
**Bearing.** With east $= r\sin\theta$ and north $= r\cos\theta$, the ship ends about {cx:num2} km east and {cy:num2} km north of the start, so the bearing is about **{brg:num1}°** (measured clockwise from north).

drills.title: Golden ratio lengths

choices.label: Find the length of a diagonal of a regular pentagon whose sides have length
Find the long side of a golden rectangle whose short side is
Find the short side of a golden rectangle whose long side is

drills.prompt: {mode} {s}. Give the answer to 2 decimal places.
drills.solution: $\varphi = \tfrac{1 + \sqrt5}{2} \approx 1.6180$. A pentagon's diagonal is $\varphi$ times its side, and a golden rectangle's long side is $\varphi$ times its short side. Going from a longer length to a shorter one, divide by $\varphi$ (or multiply by $\varphi - 1 \approx 0.618$). The answer is **{ans:num2}**.

drills.title: Power of a point and tangent length
drills.prompt: Find the power of $P({px}, {py})$ with respect to the circle $x^2 + y^2 {D:signedcoef}x {E:signedcoef}y {F:signed} = 0$, and the length of a tangent segment from $P$ (exact, like sqrt(20), or 2 decimals).
drills.solution: Substitute $P$ into the left side: $({px})^2 + ({py})^2 + ({D})({px}) + ({E})({py}) + ({F}) =$ **{pw}**. It's positive, so $P$ is outside, and the tangent length is $\sqrt{{pw}} \approx$ **{t:num2}**. (Check: the center is $({h}, {k})$ and $r^2 = {r2}$; $P$'s squared distance from the center is ${d2}$, and ${d2} - {r2} = {pw}$.)

drills.title: Radical axis and common chord
drills.prompt: The circles $x^2 + y^2 = {r1sq}$ and $(x - {dd})^2 + y^2 = {r2sq}$ cross at two points. Their radical axis is a vertical line $x = c$. Find $c$ and the length of the common chord (exact or 2 decimals).
drills.solution: General forms: $x^2 + y^2 - {r1sq} = 0$ and $x^2 + y^2 - {d2}x {k2:signed} = 0$. Subtracting the second from the first cancels $x^2$ and $y^2$: ${d2}x = {num}$, so $c = \dfrac{{num}}{{d2}} \approx$ **{c:num2}**. On that line the first circle gives $y^2 = {r1sq} - c^2$, so $y = \pm\sqrt{{r1sq} - c^2} \approx \pm{half:num4}$, and the common chord is $2\sqrt{{r1sq} - c^2} \approx$ **{chord:num2}**.

drills.title: Circumradius from the Law of Sines
drills.prompt: In $\triangle ABC$, side $a = {side}$, $m\angle A = {angA}^\circ$ and $m\angle B = {angB}^\circ$. Find the circumradius $R$ and side $b$ (2 decimals).
drills.solution: Extended Law of Sines: $2R = \dfrac{a}{\sin A} = \dfrac{{side}}{\sin {angA}^\circ} \approx {twoR:num4}$, so $R \approx$ **{R:num2}**. Then $b = 2R\sin B \approx {twoR:num4} \cdot \sin {angB}^\circ \approx$ **{b:num2}**. (Keep $2R$ unrounded until the end.)

drills.title: Circumradius of an isosceles triangle
drills.prompt: An isosceles triangle has base {base} and height {hh} to that base. Find the radius of its circumscribed circle (exact fraction or 2 decimals).
drills.solution: The height bisects the base, so each leg is $\sqrt{{m}^2 + {hh}^2} = \sqrt{{l2}}$. The area is $K = \tfrac12 \cdot {base} \cdot {hh} = {K}$. Then $R = \dfrac{abc}{4K} = \dfrac{\sqrt{{l2}} \cdot \sqrt{{l2}} \cdot {base}}{4 \cdot {K}} = \dfrac{{l2}}{{h2}} \approx$ **{R:num2}**.

drills.title: The circle through three points
drills.prompt: Find the center $(h, k)$ and radius $r$ of the circle through $({x1}, {y1})$, $({x2}, {y2})$ and $({x3}, {y3})$.
drills.solution: Substitute each point into $x^2 + y^2 + Dx + Ey + F = 0$. Subtracting the equations in pairs cancels $F$ and leaves two linear equations in $D$ and $E$; solving gives $D = {D}$ and $E = {E}$, and then any one equation gives $F = {F}$. So the circle is $x^2 + y^2 {D:signedcoef}x {E:signedcoef}y {F:signed} = 0$. Completing the square: $(x {nh:signed})^2 + (y {nk:signed})^2 = {r2}$. Center **({h}, {k})**, radius $\sqrt{{r2}} =$ **{r}**. (Or intersect the perpendicular bisectors of two of the segments, as in Lesson 15.)

drills.title: Vertices, edges and faces of prisms, pyramids and bipyramids
drills.prompt: Count the vertices, edges and faces of a {kind} whose base is a polygon with {n} sides. (A bipyramid is two pyramids glued base to base.)
drills.solution: For a base with $n$ sides: a prism has $V = 2n$, $E = 3n$, $F = n + 2$ (two copies of the base, joined by $n$ side faces); a pyramid has $V = n + 1$, $E = 2n$, $F = n + 1$ (the base plus an apex); a bipyramid has $V = n + 2$, $E = 3n$, $F = 2n$ (two apexes, $n$ triangles on each side). Here the {kind} has $V =$ **{V}**, $E =$ **{E}** and $F =$ **{F}**. Check with Euler's formula: ${V} - {E} + {F} = 2$.

drills.prompt: Every vertex of a convex polyhedron looks the same: {config} meet there. Find the angle defect at each vertex (in degrees) and the number of vertices.
drills.solution: Interior angles: triangle $60^\circ$, square $90^\circ$, pentagon $108^\circ$, hexagon $120^\circ$, octagon $135^\circ$, decagon $144^\circ$. The angles at each vertex add to ${angsum}^\circ$, so the defect is $360^\circ - {angsum}^\circ =$ **{d}°**. By Descartes' theorem all the defects add to $720^\circ$, so there are $720 \div {d} =$ **{V}** vertices.

drills.title: Volume of a frustum of a cone
drills.prompt: A frustum of a cone has bottom radius {R}, top radius {r} and height {h}. Find its volume (exact, like 3800pi, or to 2 decimal places).
drills.solution: $V = \dfrac{\pi h}{3}\left(R^2 + Rr + r^2\right) = \dfrac{\pi \cdot {h}}{3}\left({R2:dp0} + {Rr:dp0} + {r2:dp0}\right) = \dfrac{{h} \cdot {S3:dp0}}{3}\pi = {k:dp0}\pi \approx$ **{V:num2}**.

drills.title: Volume and curved area of a spherical cap
drills.prompt: A plane cuts a cap of height {h} from a sphere of radius {R}. Find the cap's volume and the area of its curved surface (exact, like 48pi, or to 2 decimal places).
drills.solution:
Volume: $V = \dfrac{\pi h^2}{3}(3R - h) = \dfrac{\pi \cdot {h2:dp0}}{3}({t:dp0}) = {k:dp0}\pi \approx$ **{V:num2}**.
Curved area (Archimedes' hat-box theorem): $S = 2\pi R h = 2\pi \cdot {R} \cdot {h} = {kS:dp0}\pi \approx$ **{S:num2}**.

drills.title: Volume and surface area of a torus (Pappus)
drills.prompt: A circle of radius {r} is spun around an axis in its plane, {R} units from its center. Find the volume and surface area of the torus it sweeps out (to 2 decimal places).
drills.solution: The centroid (the circle's center) travels $2\pi \cdot {R}$. Volume $=$ area × distance $= \pi \cdot {r2} \cdot 2\pi \cdot {R} = {kV:dp0}\pi^2 \approx$ **{V:num2}**. Surface area $=$ circumference × distance $= 2\pi \cdot {r} \cdot 2\pi \cdot {R} = {kS:dp0}\pi^2 \approx$ **{S:num2}**.

drills.title: Largest pen against a wall
drills.prompt: You have {P} m of fence for a rectangular pen against a long straight wall, so only three sides need fence. Find the width (each side touching the wall), the length (the side parallel to the wall) and the largest possible area.
drills.solution: With width $W$ and length $L$, the fence gives $L + 2W = {P:dp0}$. By AM–GM the product $L \cdot 2W$ is largest when $L = 2W$, so $4W = {P:dp0}$: $W =$ **{W}** m and $L =$ **{L}** m. Area $= {L:dp0} \times {W:dp0} =$ **{A}** m².

drills.title: Regular polygon with a given perimeter
drills.prompt: A regular {n}-gon has perimeter {P}. Find its area (to 2 decimal places) and its isoperimetric quotient $Q = \dfrac{4\pi A}{P^2}$ (to 3 decimal places).
drills.solution: Each side is $\tfrac{{P}}{{n}}$ and the apothem is $\dfrac{s/2}{\tan(180^\circ/n)}$, so $A = \dfrac{P^2}{4n\tan(180^\circ/n)} = \dfrac{{P}^2}{4 \cdot {n} \cdot \tan {half:num2}^\circ} \approx$ **{A:num2}**. Then $Q = \dfrac{4\pi A}{P^2} = \dfrac{\pi}{{n}\tan {half:num2}^\circ} \approx$ **{Q:dp3}**. (A circle with the same perimeter would enclose $\tfrac{P^2}{4\pi} \approx {Acirc:dp2}$, with $Q = 1$.)

drills.title: The can that uses the least metal
drills.prompt: A closed cylindrical can must hold {V} cm³. Find the radius and height that use the least metal (to 2 decimal places), and that least surface area (to the nearest whole cm²).
drills.solution: The best can has $h = 2r$, so $V = \pi r^2 h = 2\pi r^3$: $r = \sqrt[3]{\dfrac{{V:dp0}}{2\pi}} \approx$ **{r:num2}** cm and $h = 2r \approx$ **{h:num2}** cm. Then $S = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi r h = 6\pi r^2 \approx$ **{S:num2}** cm², about {S:dp0} cm².

drills.title: Two reflections make a rotation
drills.prompt: A figure is reflected in the line through the origin that makes an angle of ${al}^\circ$ with the positive $x$-axis, and then in the line through the origin at ${be}^\circ$. The result is a rotation about the origin. Through what counterclockwise angle, between $0^\circ$ and $360^\circ$?
drills.solution:
A reflection in a line through the origin at angle $\alpha$ keeps each point's distance from $O$ and sends its angle $\varphi$ to $2\alpha - \varphi$. Two in a row: $\varphi \to 2\beta - (2\alpha - \varphi) = \varphi + 2(\beta - \alpha)$.
Here $2({be} - {al}) = 2({df}) = {r}$ degrees. A turn of ${r}^\circ$ is the same as one of ${ang}^\circ$ counterclockwise (add $360^\circ$ to a negative angle), so the answer is **{ang}°**.

drills.title: Reflect, then translate
drills.prompt: Reflect in the line $y = {k}$, then translate by $\langle {a}, {b} \rangle$. The result is a glide reflection: a reflection in a horizontal line $y = m$ followed by a slide of $t$ units along that line (positive means to the right). Find $m$ and $t$.
drills.solution:
Reflecting in $y = {k}$ sends $(x, y)$ to $(x,\; 2({k}) - y)$; the translation then gives $(x {a:signed},\; {kk2} - y)$.
A point's $y$-coordinate and its image's always average $\tfrac{{kk2}}{2} = {m}$, so the mirror of the glide reflection is $y =$ **{m}** (the vertical part of the translation just moves the mirror by half of it). The horizontal part is the slide: $t =$ **{t}**.

drills.title: Rotate a point by any angle
drills.prompt: Rotate $({x}, {y})$ by ${th}^\circ$ counterclockwise about the origin. Give each coordinate to 2 decimal places.
drills.solution:
$\cos {th}^\circ \approx {cs:num4}$ and $\sin {th}^\circ \approx {sn:num4}$.
$x' = x\cos\theta - y\sin\theta = ({x})({cs:num4}) - ({y})({sn:num4}) \approx$ **{xr:num2}**.
$y' = x\sin\theta + y\cos\theta = ({x})({sn:num4}) + ({y})({cs:num4}) \approx$ **{yr:num2}**.

drills.title: Apply a matrix to a point
drills.prompt: Find the image of the point $({x}, {y})$ under the matrix $\begin{bmatrix} {a} & {b} \\ {c} & {d} \end{bmatrix}$.

drills.title: Determinant and area of an image
drills.prompt: The triangle with vertices $(0, 0)$, $({p}, 0)$ and $(0, {q})$ is transformed by the matrix $\begin{bmatrix} {a} & {b} \\ {c} & {d} \end{bmatrix}$. Find the determinant of the matrix and the area of the image triangle.
drills.solution:
$\det = ({a})({d}) - ({b})({c}) =$ **{det}**.
The original triangle has area $\tfrac12 \cdot {p} \cdot {q} = {ar0}$. Every area is multiplied by $|\det|$, so the image has area $|{det}| \cdot {ar0} =$ **{ar1}**. (A negative determinant also means the image has the opposite orientation.)

drills.title: Foci of an ellipse
drills.prompt: For the ellipse $\dfrac{(x {nh:signed})^2}{{d1}} + \dfrac{(y {nk:signed})^2}{{d2}} = 1$, find $c$, the distance from the center to each focus, and the coordinates of the focus that lies to the right of or above the center.
drills.solution:
The center is $({h}, {k})$. The larger denominator, $a^2 = {a2}$, is under the ${dir}$-term, so the major axis (and both foci) run parallel to the ${dir}$-axis; the other denominator is $b^2 = {b2}$.
$c^2 = a^2 - b^2 = {a2} - {b2} = {c2}$, so $c =$ **{cc}**. Moving {cc} from the center along the major axis (right or up) gives the focus **({fx}, {fy})**.

drills.title: Ellipse from its foci
drills.prompt: An ellipse has foci $({f1x}, {f1y})$ and $({f2x}, {f2y})$, and for every point on it the distances to the two foci add up to {s}. Its equation is $\dfrac{(x {nh:signed})^2}{A} + \dfrac{(y {nk:signed})^2}{B} = 1$. Find $A$ and $B$.
drills.solution:
The center is the midpoint of the foci, $({h}, {k})$, and each focus is $c = {cc}$ from it. The sum is $2a = {s}$, so $a = {aa}$ and $b^2 = a^2 - c^2 = {a2} - {c2} = {b2}$.
The foci lie on a line parallel to the ${dir}$-axis, so $a^2 = {a2}$ goes under the ${dir}$-term: $A =$ **{d1}** and $B =$ **{d2}**.

drills.title: Hyperbola from its foci
drills.prompt: A hyperbola has foci $(-{cc}, 0)$ and $({cc}, 0)$, and for every point on it the distances to the two foci differ by {s}. Its equation is $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2} - \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} = 1$. Find $b^2$ and the positive slope of the asymptotes (as a fraction or to 2 decimal places).
drills.solution:
The difference is $2a = {s}$, so $a = {aa}$, and $c = {cc}$. For a hyperbola $b^2 = c^2 - a^2 = {c2} - {a2} =$ **{b2}**, so $b = {bb}$.
The asymptotes are $y = \pm\tfrac{b}{a}x = \pm\tfrac{{bb}}{{aa}}x$, so the positive slope is $\tfrac{{bb}}{{aa}} \approx$ **{sl:num2}**.
